description: UI + state wiring for the Reassign decision. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 (types, reassignReviewItem, searchIdentities, PluginRuntime.searchApi, reassign presets, and the metrics/priority 'resolved' decision must already exist). Adds the reusable accessible IdentityPicker, extends DecisionDialog with a reassign mode (person picker + required preset-or-custom comment), extends useDecisions/useReviewItems with an optimistic reassign path, adds the third 'Reassign' action/badge to the card, surfaces 'Reassigned' in the drill-down table, and threads runtime.searchApi + confirmReassign through CertApp. Includes the full UI/hook test suite.
steps: src/components/IdentityPicker.tsx + .css (NEW): a reusable searchable combobox. Props `{ searchApi: SearchApi; value: IdentityOption | null; onChange: (v: IdentityOption | null) => void; disabled?: boolean }`. Debounce the text input ~275ms (small inline useEffect+setTimeout or a tiny useDebouncedValue hook); do not call searchIdentities for <2 chars. Render input with role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant; results in a role=listbox with role=option items (stable ids); support ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter/Escape; show distinct loading, empty ('No matches'), and error states; when a value is selected show the person's displayName+email with a 'Clear' button. Use existing `vc-` CSS naming conventions. Call `searchIdentities(searchApi, query)` from FEAT-001.

src/components/DecisionDialog.tsx + .css: add a `searchApi?: SearchApi` prop and an `onConfirmReassign?: (identityId: string, comment: string) => void` prop. When `choice === 'reassign'`: render the IdentityPicker ABOVE the existing preset-or-custom comment control (reuse the current comment combobox logic unchanged; the reassign comment is always required), keep local state for the selected IdentityOption, and enable Confirm only when BOTH an identity is selected AND the comment is non-empty; the confirm button calls onConfirmReassign(selected.id, comment). Keep the allow/remove branches and their onConfirm path untouched. Title/meaning text come from the FEAT-001 language entries (DECISION_LABEL/DECISION_MEANING['reassign']). Give the reassign confirm button its own class (e.g. vc-btn-reassign) and plain label 'Reassign'.

src/state/useReviewItems.ts: add `applyReassign(itemId: string, comments: string | null)` alongside applyDecision/revertDecision that marks the item `{ completed: true, reassigned: true, comments }` optimistically; `revertDecision` must also clear `reassigned` back to false. Expose applyReassign on ReviewItemsState.

src/state/useDecisions.ts: widen PendingDecision/open to allow `choice: 'reassign'` and add `confirmReassign(identityId: string, comment: string)` that: optimistically calls `review.applyReassign(item.id, comment.trim() || null)`, calls `reassignReviewItem(api, { certificationId: campaignId, itemId: item.id, reassignToId: identityId, reason: comment.trim() })`, then `onCampaignUpdated(updated)` and closes the dialog; on failure calls `review.revertDecision(item.id)` and sets the same FriendlyError message as the keep/remove path. Keep the existing confirm(comment) for allow/remove.

src/components/ReviewItemCard.tsx + .css: add a third button 'Reassign' (onDecide('reassign')) in the undecided actions row, and render a 'Reassigned' badge (styled like the Kept/Removed badges) plus the comment and a 'Change' affordance when `item.reassigned` is true. Make sure the decided/resolved branch recognizes reassigned items.
src/components/ReviewQueue.tsx: no signature change needed because onDecide now accepts the widened DecisionChoice; verify the prop type flows through.
src/components/DrillDownTable.tsx: show 'Reassigned' in the Decision column when item.reassigned is true (before the APPROVE/REVOKE/Not decided checks).

src/CertApp.tsx: pass `runtime.searchApi` into the rendered <DecisionDialog searchApi={...} onConfirmReassign={decisions.confirmReassign} .../>; handleDecide already opens the dialog for any choice so it only needs to accept 'reassign'. Ensure ReviewView's outstanding/allDecided counts (which filter on item.completed) now also treat reassigned items as resolved — they will, since applyReassign sets completed:true.

Tests (new): src/components/IdentityPicker.test.tsx — debounced search fires searchIdentities, keyboard navigation selects an option, selection calls onChange, loading/empty/error states render, combobox/listbox/option roles present. Tests (extend): src/components/DecisionDialog.test.tsx (reassign mode keeps Confirm disabled until BOTH identity and comment chosen, then calls onConfirmReassign with id+comment), src/state/useDecisions.test.ts (confirmReassign optimistically applies, calls reassignReviewItem, refreshes campaign, rolls back + friendly error on failure), src/components/ReviewQueue.test.tsx (third Reassign button calls onDecide with 'reassign'), src/CertApp.test.tsx (buildRuntime gains searchApi mock; dialog receives it). Mock SearchApi/CertificationsApi with the existing `as unknown as` fakeApi pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Each review item shows three actions — Keep access, Remove access, Reassign — and reassigned items render a 'Reassigned' badge and leave the outstanding queue.

The reassign dialog requires BOTH a selected identity (via the searchable picker) AND a non-empty comment before Confirm is enabled, and on confirm calls reassignReviewItem with the certification id, item id, chosen identity id, and comment.
IdentityPicker is keyboard-operable with combobox/listbox/option roles and debounces input (~275ms), not querying for <2 chars.
`npm test` passes with the new and extended tests (IdentityPicker, DecisionDialog reassign, useDecisions reassign, ReviewQueue third button, CertApp searchApi).
`npm run lint` is clean and `npm run build` succeeds.
verification: npx vitest run src/components src/state src/CertApp.test.tsx
findings:
FEAT-002 landed. Integration/review reference.

NEW FILES:
- src/components/IdentityPicker.tsx (+ .css): reusable searchable combobox. Props { searchApi: SearchApi; value: IdentityOption | null; onChange: (v) => void; disabled?: boolean }. Debounces input 275ms (DEBOUNCE_MS const) and never searches for <2 non-space chars. a11y: input role=combobox with aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-activedescendant/aria-autocomplete='list'; results in role=listbox with role=option items (stable ids `${useId}-${option.id}`), aria-selected on the active option. Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown wrap through options (first result auto-active), Enter selects active, Escape closes list. States: 'Searching…' / 'No matches' (role status) / error (role=alert, FriendlyError message). When value set, renders selected name+email with a 'Clear' button (vc-link-btn) and hides the combobox. IMPORTANT lint note: the search effect defers ALL setState into queueMicrotask() to satisfy the react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rule (ESLint 10 flat config flags synchronous setState in an effect body) — keep that shape if editing.

EDITED SOURCE:
- DecisionDialog.tsx (+ .css): added optional props searchApi?: SearchApi and onConfirmReassign?: (identityId, comment) => void. When choice==='reassign': renders IdentityPicker ABOVE the (reused, unchanged) preset-or-custom comment control; comment is ALWAYS required in reassign mode (required = isReassign || commentRequired(...)); Confirm enabled only when recipient !== null AND comment.length > 0; confirm button class vc-btn-reassign, label 'Reassign', onClick calls onConfirmReassign(recipient.id, comment). allow/remove onConfirm path untouched. Added data-choice='reassign' meaning style (accent bg).
- useReviewItems.ts: added applyReassign(itemId, comments) → sets { completed:true, reassigned:true, comments }; revertDecision now also clears reassigned:false. applyReassign exposed on ReviewItemsState (any future ReviewItemsState mock/fixture must include it — currently only useDecisions.test.ts builds one).
- useDecisions.ts: added confirmReassign(identityId, comment) → optimistic review.applyReassign(item.id, trimmed||null), reassignReviewItem(api, { certificationId: campaignId, itemId, reassignToId: identityId, reason: trimmed }), onCampaignUpdated(updated) + close; on failure review.revertDecision(item.id) + same friendly fallback message as keep/remove. PendingDecision.choice already allowed 'reassign' (DecisionChoice), so open() needed no change.
- ReviewItemCard.tsx (+ .css): third 'Reassign' button (vc-btn-reassign) in the undecided actions row; decided branch now recognizes reassigned items — badge 'Reassigned' (vc-decided-reassign, accent), comment shown, 'Change' re-opens choice 'reassign'. data-decided attr is 'reassign' for reassigned items.
- DrillDownTable.tsx: Decision cell shows 'Reassigned' before the APPROVE/REVOKE/Not decided checks.
- CertApp.tsx: destructures searchApi from runtime and passes searchApi={searchApi} onConfirmReassign={decisions.confirmReassign} to <DecisionDialog>. ReviewView outstanding/allDecided counts filter on item.completed, which applyReassign sets true, so reassigned items leave the queue automatically (no ReviewView change needed).
- ReviewQueue.tsx: no change (onDecide already typed DecisionChoice).

TESTS: IdentityPicker.test.tsx (8 new: roles/debounce, <2-char no-search, keyboard select, click select, empty, loading, error, selected+Clear) — mocks '../sailpoint/identities' searchIdentities, keeps real FriendlyError. DecisionDialog.test.tsx (+2 reassign-mode tests, mocks searchIdentities). useDecisions.test.ts (+2 confirmReassign tests; makeReview() mock now includes applyReassign; asserts ReviewReassign body { reassign:[{id, type:'ITEM'}], reassignTo, reason }). ReviewQueue.test.tsx (asserts third Reassign button → onDecide('r1','reassign')). CertApp.test.tsx (buildRuntime + full-flow runtime now carry searchApi; new test drives dashboard→review→Reassign→picker types→runtime searchPostV1 called, proving searchApi reached the dialog; uses the REAL searchIdentities/picker against the fake searchApi).

VERIFICATION (all green): npx vitest run src/components src/state src/CertApp.test.tsx = 38; npm test = 93 (FEAT-001 left it at 80, +13 new here); npm run lint clean; npm run build OK. No git repo — nothing committed. No deviations; no user-visible behavior changed beyond the stated reassign feature.
